blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A cost curve has breakpoints (0, 0), (10, 50) and (20, 70). It is written as x = 10 l1 + 20 l2, y = 50 l1 + 70 l2, l0 + l1 + l2 = 1 and every l >= 0, with no other rows. The model minimizes y with x fixed at 10. Which y does it report?

options.text: 50, the curve's value, as x sits on the middle breakpoint
options.says: Putting all weight on the middle breakpoint gives 50, but half on each end also gives x = 10, with y = 35, and the solver wants y small.

options.text: 70, the last breakpoint's value, as the weights add up to one
options.says: All weight on the last breakpoint gives x = 20, not 10, so it is not allowed here.

options.text: 35, half the last breakpoint's value, from weights on both ends
options.says: Right: l0 = l2 = 0.5 gives x = 10 and y = 35, a point on the chord below the curve, as the weights-only rows allowed on GridCap.

options.text: 0, the first breakpoint's value, as nothing pushes the weights up
options.says: All weight on the first breakpoint gives x = 0, not 10; the weights must reproduce the fixed x.

origin.section: Weights on the Breakpoints Describe Every Point of the Curve

questions.stem: A curve has breakpoints 0, 1, 2 and 3, segment k running from breakpoint k-1 to breakpoint k, and segment binaries z1, z2, z3 with z1 + z2 + z3 = 1. Which row limits the weight l2 on breakpoint 2?

options.says: Right: breakpoint 2 ends segment 2 and starts segment 3, so it may carry weight when either is chosen.
With segment 3 chosen this row forbids weight on breakpoint 2, the left end of segment 3, so the points of segment 3 are lost.
The right side is always 1, so the row never limits l2, and weights on non-neighbours stay allowed.
Breakpoint 2 is not on segment 1, and the row forbids it on segment 3, which it starts.

origin.section: One Binary per Segment Enforces the Neighbour Rule

questions.stem: A tariff curve has breakpoints at 0, 100, 250 and 400 MWh, with segment binaries z1 (0 to 100), z2 (100 to 250) and z3 (250 to 400). A permit p is written as p >= z3. What does the model require for a purchase of exactly 250 MWh?

options.text: A permit, since 250 MWh is where segment 3 starts
options.says: 250 MWh also ends segment 2, and with z2 = 1 the row p >= z3 asks nothing.

options.text: A permit, since z2 and z3 both equal 1 at a breakpoint
options.says: Exactly one segment binary is 1, because the binaries add up to 1.

options.text: No purchase, since a breakpoint belongs to no segment
options.says: A breakpoint belongs to both segments next to it; either may be chosen.

options.text: No permit, since 250 MWh can sit at the end of segment 2
options.says: Right: at a breakpoint both neighbouring segments are allowed, so the rule reads as above 250 MWh.

origin.section: The Segment Binaries Are Decisions Other Rules Can Use

concepts: the row that limits one breakpoint's weight
a rule triggered by a segment, read at a breakpoint
a cost written as breakpoint weights with no other rows
